sections.heading: Section 1: The Poisson Probability Mass Function

questions.q: If $X \sim \text{Po}(\lambda)$, what is the probability mass function $P(X = k)$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, \dots$?
questions.answer: The Poisson probability mass function is given by $P(X = k) = \frac{e^{-\lambda} \lambda^k}{k!}$ for $k \in \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$.

questions.q: A call center receives an average of $3$ calls per minute ($X \sim \text{Po}(3)$). What is the probability of receiving exactly $2$ calls in a given minute?

sections.heading: Section 2: Mean, Variance, and Poisson Characteristics

questions.q: What is a distinctive mathematical property of any Poisson random variable $X \sim \text{Po}(\lambda)$?
choices: The mean and variance are strictly equal: $E(X) = \text{Var}(X) = \lambda$
questions.answer: A defining feature of the Poisson distribution is that its expected value and variance are both equal to the rate parameter $\lambda$.

questions.q: If a Poisson random variable has variance $\text{Var}(X) = 16$, what is its standard deviation?
Under what practical conditions does a Poisson process serve as a valid model?
choices: Events occur independently, singly, and at a constant average rate across continuous time or space
There are exactly two trials with equal probability
Events must occur in clusters at predetermined times
The probability of an event increases as time elapses
questions.answer: A Poisson process assumes events happen independently at a constant average rate, without simultaneous multiple arrivals.

sections.heading: Section 3: Changing Time Intervals & Sum of Independent Poisson RVs

questions.q: Flaws on a wire occur at an average rate of $1.5$ per meter. What is the distribution of flaws $Y$ in a $4$-meter segment of wire?
questions.answer: Poisson rates scale linearly with interval size: $\lambda_{\text{new}} = 1.5 \times 4 = 6$. Thus $Y \sim \text{Po}(6)$.

questions.q: If $X \sim \text{Po}(4)$ and $Y \sim \text{Po}(7)$ are independent random variables, what is the distribution of $W = X + Y$?
questions.answer: The sum of independent Poisson random variables is itself a Poisson random variable whose parameter is the sum of the individual rates: $\lambda_W = 4 + 7 = 11$.

questions.q: If $W \sim \text{Po}(11)$, what is the variance of $W$?

sections.heading: Section 4: Poisson Approximation to the Binomial Distribution

questions.q: When can a Binomial distribution $B(n, p)$ be well approximated by a Poisson distribution $\text{Po}(\lambda)$?
choices: When $n$ is very large ($n > 50$) and $p$ is very small ($p < 0.1$), with $\lambda = np$
questions.answer: The Poisson distribution is the limiting form of the Binomial distribution as $n \to \infty$ and $p \to 0$ such that $np = \lambda$ remains moderate.

questions.q: A factory produces microchips with defect probability $p = 0.002$. In a batch of $n = 1000$ chips, approximate the probability of finding zero defects.
